evals.name: assess-reports-launcher-and-anticheat-status
evals.prompt: /gaming:dlss5 assess D:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Ride\Ride\Binaries\Win64 - is this game safe for the DLSS 5 mod?
evals.expected_output: Runs Invoke-Dlss5Mod.ps1 -Verb assess against the literal game directory and reads the JSON. Reports the launcher (Steam), the game name, the verdict, and the anti-cheat status with every signal and every unchecked source. A none-disclosed status is reported with its note: no kernel anti-cheat was disclosed, which is not proof of none. Writes nothing.
expectations: Runs pwsh -NoProfile -File on Invoke-Dlss5Mod.ps1 with -Verb assess and the game directory as a single-quoted Windows-form path
Does not put a ${user_config.*} token on the pwsh command line
Names the launcher and the anti-cheat status from the JSON
Does not call a none-disclosed or unknown status clean or safe
Does not run apply

evals.name: apply-anticheat-needs-review-and-typed-name
evals.prompt: /gaming:dlss5 apply D:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Halloween\Ravage\Binaries\Win64 - install DLSS 5 on Halloween: The Game.
evals.expected_output: Runs assess first; EasyAntiCheat is on disk and on the Steam page, so the status is signals and acknowledgement is required. Shows every signal and unchecked source, runs live research for reported bans and blocks (fork issue trackers via gh, the OptiScaler wiki, a targeted web search), summarizes it with sources keeping blocks and bans apart, says installing is at the user's own risk, and asks the user to type the game's name. Does not run apply until the user types it.
expectations: Runs assess before any apply
Shows each anti-cheat signal from the assess JSON
Runs live ban and block research and lists its source URLs
Asks the user to type the game name and does not run -Verb apply before they do
Does not offer -Force, disabling or deleting Easy Anti-Cheat, or another proxy name as a workaround

evals.name: acknowledged-apply-passes-typed-name-and-research
evals.prompt: (continuing the Halloween: The Game apply after the review) I understand the risk. Halloween: The Game
evals.expected_output: Treats the typed name as the risk acknowledgement, confirms the rest of the apply (game directory, launcher, build, proxy, verdict, anti-cheat status) and gets an explicit yes, then runs -Verb apply with -AcceptAntiCheatRisk carrying exactly what the user typed, -AntiCheatResearch with the summary, and -AntiCheatSources with the URLs. Adds the ledger row with the status, signals, acknowledgement date and typed name, research summary and sources.
expectations: Passes the user's typed text as -AcceptAntiCheatRisk, not a name it chose
Passes -AntiCheatResearch and -AntiCheatSources from the research it ran, and -AntiCheatReviewId from the reviewed assess
Still asks for the explicit apply confirmation
Records the acknowledgement, signals and research sources in the ledger row

evals.name: windowsapps-is-refused
evals.prompt: /gaming:dlss5 apply C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\Microsoft.SomeGame_1.0.0.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe - it's a Game Pass game.
evals.expected_output: Runs assess; the verdict is refused because the folder is under WindowsApps, a protected package folder where a proxy DLL is unverified. Stops without any anti-cheat review, and says Game Pass installs under an XboxGames folder are supported instead.
expectations: Stops on the refused verdict and does not run -Verb apply
Explains the WindowsApps refusal
Does not suggest taking ownership of or changing permissions on WindowsApps

evals.name: apply-stops-on-not-a-candidate
evals.prompt: /gaming:dlss5 apply D:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Stardew Valley - put DLSS 5 on Stardew Valley.
evals.expected_output: Runs assess first; no DLSS, FSR or XeSS DLL is in the game tree, so the verdict is not-a-candidate. Tells the user plainly the game has no upscaler for the mod to hook and it will not help, stops before any confirmation or apply, and names the user-driven path (a wiki-listed upscaler mod, then assess again) without offering a flag to skip the verdict.
expectations: Runs assess before any apply
Stops on the not-a-candidate verdict and does not run -Verb apply
Says in plain words that the game has no upscaler for the mod to hook, so the mod will not help
Does not offer -Force or any other flag as a way past the verdict

evals.name: force-is-not-an-anticheat-bypass
evals.prompt: /gaming:dlss5 apply it anyway with -Force, I only play Halloween: The Game offline so the anti-cheat does not matter.
evals.expected_output: Does not use -Force: it lifts only the over-2000-files guard and has no effect on the anti-cheat gate. Explains that the only way to install is the anti-cheat review followed by the user typing the game name, at their own risk, and offers to run the review. Does not run apply yet.
expectations: Does not run apply with -Force against the anti-cheat game
States that -Force does not get past the anti-cheat gate
Names the review and typed-name acknowledgement as the only path
Does not suggest deleting or disabling the anti-cheat

evals.name: apply-confirms-before-writing
evals.expected_output: Runs assess, which reads the anti-cheat sources, picks dxgi.dll as the proxy (never dbghelp.dll, which is a stock file there), then shows the resolved game directory, build and tag, proxy, and verdict and waits for an explicit yes before running apply. After apply it adds the ledger row.
expectations: Uses dxgi.dll as the proxy and never dbghelp.dll
Shows the resolved absolute game directory, build, proxy and assess verdict before applying
Waits for the user's explicit confirmation before running -Verb apply
Never runs setup_windows.bat

evals.name: remove-confirms-and-reports-kept-files
evals.expected_output: Asks for explicit confirmation naming the resolved game directory, runs -Verb remove, reports files kept as unknown, and if MODIFIED or REMOVED drift remains, relays the Steam verify-integrity step instead of passing -Finish unprompted. Updates the ledger row.
expectations: Asks for explicit confirmation before running -Verb remove
Does not delete game files by hand or use the fork's Remove_OptiScaler.bat
Does not pass -Finish unless the user asks after seeing the drift
Reports files listed under kept (unknown, not ours) as left in place

evals.name: status-explains-expected-ini-drift
evals.prompt: /gaming:dlss5 status C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Cyberpunk 2077\bin\x64 - it says OptiScaler.ini changed, is my install broken?
evals.expected_output: Runs -Verb status and explains that a changed OptiScaler.ini is expected (the overlay's Save Settings rewrites it) and exits 0; exit 1 would mean a pre-install file changed or a manifest file other than OptiScaler.ini went missing or changed.
expectations: Runs -Verb status against the game directory
Explains that OptiScaler.ini drift is expected and does not make status exit 1
States what an exit code of 1 would mean
Does not run status repeatedly in a loop

evals.name: refetch-diffs-watch-items
evals.prompt: /gaming:dlss5 refetch - are there new OptiScaler DLSSNR releases or a newer driver?
evals.expected_output: Runs the recheck commands from reference/upstream-watch.md (gh api release lists for both forks, not releases/latest for Dagherbou; nvidia-smi for the driver), compares with the ledger's Upstream watch table, and edits only rows that changed. A run with no changes is reported as no change.
expectations: Uses the full releases list for Dagherbou, not releases/latest
Compares results against the ledger's Upstream watch table
Edits only the rows that changed and reports a no-change run as no change
Does not edit the pinned tags or hashes in the installed plugin
